v.why: Replacing a removed edge with a 3x3 conv reconnects the node 1 path and gains much more than swapping out skip or pool.
Adding a conv where the edge was absent gives a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
Restoring the direct input-to-output edge with a conv gains more than replacing an op that already carries signal.
Replacing pooling with a conv gains less than replacing a none edge, which contributes nothing.
Deleting a 3x3 conv loses far more accuracy than deleting a weak op such as pool.
Removing the direct skip path hurts trainability and accuracy much more than removing other ops on that edge.
Cutting the first edge when it holds a conv destroys a key feature path.
Adding a skip to an empty edge helps substantially, whereas replacing a conv with skip usually hurts.
Removing a conv from an output-feeding edge costs more than removing a pool or skip.
A direct skip to the output already supplies a good gradient path, so the extra conv on edge 5 adds less.

raw:

Most are "replacement" conditions, where the parent edge is the edited edge itself and the condition says which op gets replaced. I expect those to be the most reliable. The edge 3 and edge 5 pairing (the first hypothesis) is the one I'm least sure of.
